# ADR-001: Markup generated by JS must come from the active theme

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-04
**Deciders:** bfhp

## Context

The problem shows up in three places.

1. **Markup inside TS.** In 12 files under `assets-src`, HTML is built from strings with Bootstrap classes hard-coded. The main ones:
   - `site/app.ts`: comments, replies, the reply form, share buttons;
   - `pages/user-cards.ts`, `user-pagination.ts`, `profile.ts`, `search.ts`;
   - spinners in `blog-post-form.ts` and `app.ts`.
2. **Behavior is tied to Bootstrap too.** `site/app.ts` has `import { Toast, Modal, Tooltip } from "bootstrap"`, and `forums.ts` uses `Modal`. If a theme switches to another framework, modals and toasts simply stop working.
3. **Two sources of truth.** For example, `components/comments/comment.twig` already exists in the theme, yet `app.ts` renders the same comment again by hand.

`THEME_CONTRACT.md` already defines a loader cascade (active theme → `default` → module `views/`). If JS takes its markup from Twig, it automatically gets the same override rules.

## Options considered

| | A. Server returns HTML fragments | B. `<template>` from the theme | C. JS renderers in the theme | D. Class map in `theme.json` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| How it works | The API renders the same `.twig` as SSR and returns `{html, meta}` | The theme puts `<template data-ui="...">` in the layout; JS clones it and fills `data-slot` | The theme registers `CMS.ui.register('comment', fn)` | JS writes `ui('button.primary')`; the theme returns a class string |
| Source of truth | One (Twig) | One (Twig) | Two (Twig + JS in every theme) | Structure stays in JS |
| Switching frameworks | ✅ | ✅ | ✅, but costly | ❌ only classes change, not structure |
| Complexity | Low/medium | Medium | High for theme authors | Low |
| Downsides | HTML is heavier than JSON; cache depends on theme and locale | Conditions and loops need slot conventions | Every theme has to be written in JS; markup drifts | Solves only half the problem |

## Decision

`<template>` (B) as the main way, plus a UI adapter. Revised 2026-10-04: the
first version of this ADR rendered lists on the server (A, `?render=html`);
B was chosen instead so the API stays JSON for every consumer and needs no
theme-aware rendering.

### 1. API responses become markup through `<template>` (B)

The Twig component that renders an item on the server (a comment, a post
card, a user row) is rendered once more, with placeholder data, inside
`<template data-ui="<name>">`. The script clones it and fills the
`data-slot*` points with the JSON it received (`ui.clone()`, `ui.fill()`).

- One component per item, so a theme that overrides it (ADR-002) restyles
  both server-rendered and script-added items, with no change in JS.
- Platform templates (comments) come from `partials/js-templates.twig`,
  included by `layouts/base.twig` only where they are used. A module renders
  its own templates in its page template, next to the list they feed.
- One template per repeated item, never whole sections, so templates do not
  grow into a second copy of the page.
- Small transient states (a spinner in a button, an empty or error message)
  may stay in the script as minimal markup without framework classes.

### 2. Behavior goes through a UI adapter

JS does not import `bootstrap` directly; it calls `CMS.ui.modal.open(el)`,
`CMS.ui.toast.show(el, type)`, `CMS.ui.tooltip.init(root)`, and uses the
declarative `data-ui-*` toggles. `default` ships a native implementation
(`<dialog>`, a toast region, `title` tooltips); the `bootstrap` theme
registers `ui-bootstrap.js` through its `assets.scripts`; any other theme
registers its own. See ADR-002.

### 3. Contract

`THEME_CONTRACT.md`, "JS surface": template names and their slots, the
toggles, the adapter interface. A theme overriding a component keeps its fill
points.

The messenger (`msgr-*`) already uses its own classes and stays as it is.

## Trade-offs

- **B vs A.** A (server-rendered fragments) needs no slot contract, but the
  API gets a second, theme- and locale-dependent response format and every
  endpoint needs Twig with the theme chain. B keeps the API as is; the cost
  is the `data-slot*` contract and some placeholder markup in the page,
  limited by the rules above.
- **Why not C.** A theme on another framework would have to rewrite all
  client-side rendering in JS.
- **Why not D.** A class map cannot survive differences in markup structure,
  e.g. a Bootstrap card vs Tailwind utilities.

## Consequences

- **Easier:** switching the theme or framework doesn't touch `assets-src`,
  item markup lives in one Twig file, no HTML strings to escape by hand.
- **Harder:** components rendered as templates need fill points that themes
  must keep; conditional parts need `data-slot-optional` or separate small
  templates.
- **Revisit later:** a CI check for framework classes in `assets-src` (the
  grep checks in `THEME_CONTRACT.md`).

## Action items

1. [x] Build `CMS.ui` (adapter + `clone/fill`) with a native adapter for `default` and `bootstrap-adapter.ts` for the `bootstrap` theme; remove direct `import … from "bootstrap"` from `app.ts` and `forums.ts`.
2. [x] Add `partials/js-templates.twig`. It renders the theme's own `comment.twig`, `reply.twig` and `load-replies.twig` as templates; spinners move to it with their modules.
3. [x] Comments use the theme's `comment.twig` through `<template>` (option B) rather than `render=html`: the same file renders on the server and in the browser, with no API change.
4. [ ] Move `user-cards`, `users`, `profile`, `search`, `forums` item markup to module `<template>`s, module by module (ADR-002 plan).
5. [x] Add a "JS surface" section to `THEME_CONTRACT.md`.
6. [ ] Test: with the `default` theme active (framework-free per ADR-002), check that the DOM has no `btn`/`card` classes after AJAX loads.
